title: MCP boolean params are stringified by the chat harness dispatcher; only the `exec` sandbox preserves native JSON types
wanted_capability: Chat-harness MCP tool dispatch should preserve JSON argument types (booleans, numbers, nulls, arrays, objects) when serializing tool call arguments, OR every bbox tool with a boolean param should accept both JSON `true`/`false` and the strings "true"/"false" so call sites work regardless of dispatch path. Today the chat surface silently turns every boolean into the string "true" / "false" before the daemon sees the argument, which fails the deserialize step with no signal at the call site beyond the raw "invalid type" error.
fallback_used: Wrapped the tool call in an `exec` cell so the boolean is passed as a native JSON `true` value, not the string "true".
evidence: session:7be994da-030f-4eb3-a0c7-65a8d9121e49 - direct chat-dispatcher call to mcp__blackbox__bbox_thread_list(include_resolved: true) returned: "failed to deserialize parameters: invalid type: string 'true', expected a boolean"; same call issued from inside an `exec` JavaScript cell with the native JS boolean `true` succeeded.

This same deserialization failure recurs on the bbox_gap `evidence` parameter when called from the chat dispatcher: the array is sent as a JSON-encoded string rather than a native sequence, producing "invalid type: string [...], expected a sequence".
